agent_notes: The superscription is verse 1 in the Hebrew numbering, so every later verse is one ahead of the KJV (Hebrew 13:2 = KJV 13:1). The verse map handles it; the commentary does not belabour it.

לַמְנַצֵּחַ is glossed 'to the choirmaster' following STEPBible and the usual rendering (HALOT, BDB: piel participle of נצח, 'to be preeminent, to oversee'). The precise liturgical sense is uncertain; I say so in the commentary. The Targum's 'to praise' is a different reading.

נֶצַח is glossed 'perpetuity' and in the translations 'for ever' / 'to the end'. Meiri notes it can mean any long time; the Aramaic-influenced 'finally, utterly' is also possible. I kept 'for ever' in the dramatic layer but 'unto the end' in the literal.

Rashi's and Radak's reading of the four 'how long' as four exiles is quoted as tradition only. It is a later midrashic reading (Radak cites it from Midrash Shocher Tov), not the plain sense, and I flag it as such.

agent_notes: עֵצוֹת: Ketiv/Qere not at issue, but STEPBible's אָשִׁית is tagged H7896K. 'Set counsels in my soul' is the literal; all five English versions take it as 'take counsel', and BBE reads it as 'be in doubt'. I follow the literal and explain in the commentary.

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses כִּי אֶמּוֹט with 'if'; I take it as 'when/for', with all five versions (when I am moved). The second 'lest' in ASV (Lest mine adversaries rejoice) reads יגילו as a jussive, which the Hebrew form does not show; KJV, Webster and YLT take it as an indicative. I take it as indicative under the governing 'lest'.

agent_notes: יָגֵל is vocalized as a jussive/short form (H1523, morph Vqj3ms) so 'may it rejoice' is literal; the English versions have 'shall rejoice'. I keep the wish form in the literal layer. Hebrew verse 6 is KJV 5 and 6 together.

גָּמַל is glossed 'dealt bountifully'. The root means to deal fully with someone, for good or ill (weaning in 1 Sam 1:22 also uses it); here the object is left unstated and the sense is good. BBE's 'given me my reward' pushes toward recompense and I do not follow it.
